summary: Restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin only via /etc/cron.allow, created the opsadmin user, verified enforcement (non-listed users denied, listed users allowed), and completed the mandatory restart protocol with confirmed boot-id change and post-restart recovery of cron config and crond service.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: crond active, no /etc/cron.allow existed, empty /etc/cron.deny, opsadmin user did not exist
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' with root:root ownership and 0644 perms
Verified cron.allow enforcement: a non-listed user (operator) invoking crontab as itself was denied with 'not allowed to use this program'
Verified opsadmin (invoking crontab as itself) and root were both able to install/list/remove a crontab
Cleaned up all test crontabs, leaving /var/spool/cron empty
Captured pre-restart boot_id and crond health as baseline
Issued 'sudo -n shutdown -r now' as a backgrounded/disowned command so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed from bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07 to 944112b2-d6f2-4501-89b8-244b827ad549, proving an actual restart

Post-restart: verified crond active/enabled, /etc/cron.allow persisted with root+opsadmin, opsadmin user persisted, and re-ran functional allow/deny checks confirming the restriction survived the reboot
Cleaned up final test crontab, confirmed /var/spool/cron empty

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state before changes (crond active, cron.allow absent, opsadmin absent)
evidence.summary: Showed crond active, /usr/bin/crontab present, no /etc/cron.allow, empty /etc/cron.deny, and opsadmin user not found prior to any changes

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (opsadmin created, cron.allow configured)
evidence.summary: Created opsadmin user and wrote /etc/cron.allow containing root and opsadmin (initial root-invoked tests were later identified as flawed since root bypasses the allow check)

evidence.requirement: Enforcement proof: non-listed user denied, listed user allowed (self-invoked, not root-proxied)
evidence.summary: operator invoking crontab as itself got exit 1 'You (operator) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)'; opsadmin invoking crontab as itself succeeded and installed/listed a crontab; both cleaned up

evidence.requirement: Root retains cron access; final clean state with no lingering crontabs; crond healthy
evidence.summary: root's own crontab install/list/remove succeeded; /etc/cron.allow shows root+opsadmin; cron.deny empty; /var/spool/cron empty; crond active and enabled

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline boot identity and service health for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07, crond active, and current cron.allow contents immediately before restart
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' printed 'issuing reboot' and the ack line before the exec stream closed due to the node going down
Two consecutive polling attempts timed out while node1 was rebooting

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Node1 became reachable again with new boot_id 944112b2-d6f2-4501-89b8-244b827ad549 (different from pre-restart bf4e9cbb...) and uptime reset to 0 minutes

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron restriction, cron service, and functional enforcement
evidence.summary: crond active/enabled, /etc/cron.allow persisted with root+opsadmin, opsadmin user persisted, operator still denied crontab access, opsadmin still allowed; test crontab cleaned up leaving /var/spool/cron empty
